cues: Ammonia turns calomel black, because finely divided mercury forms.
The name calomel comes from the Greek for beautiful black.
With corrosive sublimate, tin two chloride first gives a white precipitate of calomel, and more tin chloride turns it grey as free mercury is formed.
That two stage change proves a mercuric salt.
